sections.h2: Where is North Augusta, SC, and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
North Augusta sits on the north bank of the Savannah River, directly across the state line from Augusta, Georgia. Most of the city is in western Aiken County, with a small part reaching north into Edgefield County, and it belongs to the Central Savannah River Area and the Augusta metropolitan area.

The area, elevation and 2020 counts are from the city's Wikipedia entry. Because the city straddles two counties, the county that bills your property tax depends on which side of the line the parcel falls. City government is a mayor-council system, with seven council members elected at large to staggered four-year terms, so permit and code questions go to city hall and not the county.

sections.h2: What is North Augusta's history, and why does it matter for a house sale?
sections.html:
North Augusta traces to a land company founded in the 1890s. James U. Jackson and his brother Walter formed the North Augusta Land Company with New York investors, and the company bought a 5,600-acre tract on March 24, 1890. The city was incorporated on April 11, 1906.

The Hampton Terrace Hotel, a resort the Jacksons built, opened in 1903 and burned on December 31, 1916. Much later, the Savannah River Plant was built to the south during the Cold War. The city's population nearly quadrupled, and its area grew from 772 acres to 5,139 acres.

That growth pattern left a mix of early twentieth century streets and postwar subdivisions. The Georgia Avenue and Butler Avenue Historic District is on the National Register of Historic Places, so older homes there may be worth a call to the city before you plan exterior changes.

sections.h2: What do schools, bridges and trails mean for North Augusta buyers?
sections.html:
Most North Augusta students attend Aiken County Public Schools, and the part of the city in Edgefield County is served by the Edgefield County School District. Many families also send children to private schools across the river in Georgia.

  • High schools: North Augusta High School and Fox Creek High School, an independent charter school.
  • Middle schools: North Augusta Middle, Paul Knox Middle and Highland Springs Middle.
  • Elementary schools: Hammond Hill, Belvedere, North Augusta Elementary and Mossy Creek.
  • Greeneway Trail, established in 1995, with more than 9 miles of paved trail on a former railroad line.
  • SRP Park on the Savannah River, home of the Augusta GreenJackets.

The Thirteen Street bridge, also called the James U. Jackson Memorial Bridge, carries traffic across the Savannah River to Augusta. We found no official commute figure, so we do not quote one.

sections.h2: Which counties handle North Augusta property taxes and when are they due?
sections.html:
Aiken County and the City of North Augusta both collect on the same parcel, and the schedule is different for each. The city's tax page says city property taxes are due May 1, with a 15 percent penalty after the due date. Aiken County's page says real property bills go out in the fall and are payable without penalty by January 16, with penalties added in January, February and March.

The state code sets the general window from September 30 through January 15 and a penalty sequence of 3, 7 and 5 percent at the dates it lists in Chapter 45. Because the city and county dates differ, check both before closing, and confirm any figure with the Aiken County Treasurer's office. We could not confirm Edgefield County dates from an official page, so owners in that part of the city should ask the Edgefield County offices directly.

Delinquent taxes are referred to the Delinquent Tax Collector, who is in Suite 2500 of the Government Center at 1930 University Parkway in Aiken, and the property can be sold. North Augusta holds its annual tax sale with Aiken County on the first Monday in November. Delinquent taxes must be paid before current ones are accepted, and collection costs are added as they accrue.

sections.h2: How does Aiken County assess a North Augusta home?
sections.html:
Aiken County's assessor taxes an owner-occupied home at 4 percent rather than 6 percent of its value, and the owner can claim this on one legal residence in South Carolina. Rental homes, second homes, commercial property and land above five acres may not qualify.

The county's assessor FAQ points out two details that matter when a house changes hands:

  • Reappraisal increases are capped at 15 percent of the base-year value, using 2007 as that base year.
  • When an assessable transfer occurs, the property's value can be set at current market value instead of being limited by the cap.

In practice, a buyer may see a bigger tax bill than the seller paid. If you are selling, tell the buyer that the figure on your bill may not carry over. The county site did not state an appeal deadline, so call the assessor at the Government Center if you want to challenge a value.

sections.h2: How is a North Augusta deed recorded and what does it cost?
sections.html:
Deeds for North Augusta property in Aiken County are recorded with the Register of Deeds in Suite 2100 of the Government Center, 1930 University Parkway, Aiken. The phone number is 803.642.2072. The office says it does not offer title searches, legal advice or form preparation.

Documents recorded after June 12, 2005 are electronically imaged, but they can be viewed only on computers inside the office, and earlier documents are in books. The county does not publish fee amounts on that page.

South Carolina's deed transfer fee is separate from recording charges. It is $1.85 for each $500 of value, with $1.30 going to the state and $0.55 to the county, according to Chapter 24. Deeds of distribution from an estate are not subject to it, which can help heirs.

sections.h2: What should North Augusta sellers disclose, and when does a cash sale help?
sections.html:
South Carolina requires an owner to give a buyer a written property condition disclosure unless the transfer is exempt, and fiduciary sales by an estate, a foreclosure, and an agreed written waiver are among the exemptions. As-is agreements remain allowed. The rules are in Title 27, Chapter 50.

Situations where North Augusta owners often compare a cash sale with listing:

  • A house with deferred repairs that would hold up a bank appraisal.
  • An inherited home where heirs live out of state.
  • Back taxes that are moving toward the November tax sale.
  • A rental the owner wants to stop managing.

Cash Home Buyers looks at North Augusta houses as they stand and puts any offer in writing. Whether we make one depends on the house, and you can compare it with listing before you decide.

faqs.q: What county is North Augusta in?
faqs.a: Mostly Aiken County, with a small part in Edgefield County. Your parcel's county decides who bills your property tax and where you record your deed.

faqs.q: When are North Augusta property taxes due?
faqs.a: The city's page lists May 1 with a 15 percent penalty afterward. Aiken County says real property bills are payable without penalty by January 16. Confirm both before closing.

faqs.q: When is the Aiken County tax sale?
faqs.a: North Augusta holds its annual tax sale with Aiken County on the first Monday in November, according to the city's tax page.

faqs.q: Where is a deed recorded for a North Augusta house?
faqs.a: In Aiken County, it goes to the Register of Deeds at 1930 University Parkway, Suite 2100, Aiken. Call 803.642.2072 to confirm requirements. Edgefield County parcels go to that county.

faqs.q: Will a buyer pay the same property tax I did?
faqs.a: Not always. In Aiken County an assessable transfer lets the value reset to current market value instead of being held by the 15 percent cap, so the new bill can rise.

faqs.q: Do I have to disclose problems when selling as-is?
faqs.a: You generally give the written disclosure statement unless your transfer is exempt, but state law lets both sides agree to an as-is sale.
